questions.question: What is the range of a linear map $A:V\to W$?
options: The set of vectors in $V$ not used by $A$.
The set of inputs sent to zero.
The set of outputs $Av$ obtained from vectors $v\in V$.
questions.explanation: The range is $\operatorname{range}A=\{Av:v\in V\}$, the set of all outputs actually produced in the codomain.
questions.source_support: Definition of range of a linear map.

questions.question: When is a linear map surjective?
options: When its kernel is the whole domain.
When its range equals its codomain.
When it sends every input to zero.
questions.explanation: Surjectivity means every codomain vector has a preimage, which is exactly the equality $\operatorname{range}A=W$.
questions.source_support: Relevant result: surjective iff range equals codomain.
